text:
Sam: Follow-up from the precision RFC thread. Proposal: orchestration owns per-request precision and session stickiness. Pros/cons?
Jess: +1 for a single decision plane. Key asks: clear audit trail, per-decision ids, and a way to escrow quality (so we can revert per-route quickly).
Kai: My worry is cache-affinity. If we change precision mid-session we either invalidate KV cache or keep using a mismatched cache which is risky. Need a `stickiness` concept.
Maya: Suggestion: decision includes `stickiness_token` + `stability_ttl`. Orchestrator can decide to extend stickiness for ongoing sessions. Runtime only needs small flags: precision, token, kv_action.
Andrew: How do tenants pin precision? We should allow tenant policies to set `precision_lock` and `max_degradation` per-route. Orchestration evaluates tenant lock before any heuristic.
Jess: Telemetry needed: decision_id, policy_version, stickiness_token, applied_precision, deg_score (1000-sample rolling), latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, prompt_shape_bucket.
Kai: Add `prompt_shape_bucket` to avoid applying low-bit to long, structured prompts. Also add `hysteresis_window` so decisions don't flip-flop rapidly.
Sam: Rollback model: automated rollback if deg_score > threshold for N minutes OR if kv_cache_hit_rate drops >20% and latency_p95 increases. Otherwise open Ops ticket and mark impacted tenants.
Maya: For RPC efficiency, send a compact decision token instead of full blob. Token maps to decision record in orchestration. Runtime asks orchestration for details only on cache miss.
Andrew: Compliance: store decision mapping (token -> full decision record) for Private customers, retention per their compliance needs.
Jess: We should run canaries that exercise: sticky vs non-sticky decisions, sudden precision flips, tenant-locked paths. Also run synthetic stress with mixed prompt shapes.
Kai: Test matrix: (sticky true/false) x (fp8/int8/4bit) x (short/long prompts) x (kv_cache warm/cold). Prioritize longctx x lowbit.
OpsBot: canary report: precision-stickiness-canary-5/24: 5k reqs, avg latency +4ms, deg_score median 0.022, cache_hit_rate -8% on switched sessions.
Maya: Action items: I'll draft `decision-token` API and stickiness semantics. Jess to draft telemetry schema and thresholds. Kai to prepare synthetic test harness. Sam will update RFC with new flow.
Sam: Nice. Keep runtime minimal: accept token + small flags, reuse KV when token matches, and treat runtime-only emergency fallback as a last resort with audit log.
Andrew: +1. Also capture policy precedence doc (tenant lock > route rule > hint).
Jess: I'll add monitoring alerts and a quality-escrow playbook for customer-visible regressions.
Sam: Thanks. End of thread.
